name: Ramp
text: Add one high-contrast skip link at the very top of every page that jumps straight to the main content. This fixes keyboard navigation for users who rely on assistive tech by letting them bypass repetitive navigation blocks. The trade-off is a tiny bit of extra vertical space at the top, which is negligible compared to the accessibility win.

name: Reader
text: A single high-contrast skip link fails users who rely on screen readers when the target `<main role="main">` isn’t programmatically exposed or when the page reflows dynamically—screen readers may land in a dead zone. Instead, pair it with a visible skip link *and* ensure every page has a clearly labeled `<main>` element with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to guarantee reliable focus. Test with a screen reader and keyboard only; if focus jumps unpredictably, the pattern is broken.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a high-contrast skip link *and* ensure every page has a clearly labeled `<main>` landmark with `role="main"`—no exceptions. This covers both keyboard users who need to bypass blocks and screen reader users who rely on landmarks to orient themselves. The trade-off is a small markup change on every page, but it eliminates dead zones and makes navigation predictable for everyone.

name: Reader
text: A visible skip link *and* `<main role="main">` still fails when dynamic content loads after the initial render—screen readers may not announce the new main content, leaving users trapped in a dead zone. The real fix is pairing the skip link with ARIA live regions that announce dynamic updates, plus testing with actual screen readers to confirm the flow. Settle it by running a test with NVDA or VoiceOver on a page that loads content via AJAX—if the user can’t reach the new main content, the pattern is broken.
